cards.title: Google DeepMind Releases Gemini 3.7 Flash: Major Coding and Agent Benchmark Gains at Half the Price
cards.why_it_matters: As a likely user of Gemini API models for agent workflows and coding tasks, the jump in SWE-bench-style scores and halved pricing makes this an immediate practical upgrade to evaluate.
cards.summary: Gemini 3.7 Flash, released three weeks after 3.6 Flash, shows large gains on coding benchmarks: FrontierCode 1.1 Main (43.6% vs 34.4%) and DeepSWE v1.1 (65.3% vs 49.0%). Web dev Elo on WebDev Arena rises to 1588 vs 1538. Knowledge-work benchmarks also improve: GDP.pdf (34.0% vs 22.0%) and AutomationBench (30.4% vs 17.0%). Priced at $0.75/1M input and $3.75/1M output tokens—half of 3.6 Flash's original price.

cards.title: Hugging Face Hackathon Reproduced 2,226 ICML 2026 Papers with AI Agents—Here's What They Found
cards.why_it_matters: As a researcher, the scale and methodology here—agents reproducing 34% of a top ML conference in weeks, including catching proof errors in a spotlight paper—directly concerns how you should think about paper reliability and the future of peer review.
cards.summary: A community hackathon (July 15–Aug 2, 2026) attempted reproduction of 2,226 of 6,341 accepted ICML 2026 papers using coding agents (Claude Code, Codex, Cursor, orx). Participants published 6,816 logbooks with code, artifacts, and optional full agent traces; 35,908 claims were judged by an automated GLM-5.2 judge issuing verified/falsified/toy/inconclusive verdicts. The post highlights at least one accepted spotlight paper where proofs did not survive careful checking—something the reviewer explicitly admitted skipping.

cards.title: Hugging Face + AWS Strands Robots: Closed-Loop Robot Data Pipeline with Storage Buckets
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on robot learning or embodied AI, this is a concrete end-to-end open-source blueprint for continuous collect→train→deploy loops using LeRobot, Strands Agents, and HF's new Xet-backed Storage Buckets to avoid redundant byte transfers.
cards.summary: AWS Strands Robots SDK (Apache 2.0) now integrates with Hugging Face Storage Buckets—a mutable, non-versioned, Xet-backed object store announced March 2026—to close the robot learning loop. The same Robot() factory records LeRobot-format demonstrations, syncs only changed bytes to a bucket, streams the dataset back frame-by-frame without a full download, and deploys the trained checkpoint to hardware with one argument change. LeRobot's format is already used by 90K+ datasets from 8K+ publishers on the Hub.

cards.title: Photonic Quantum SWITCH Enables BB84-Like QKD with No Key Disclosure for Eavesdropping Detection
cards.why_it_matters: For anyone tracking quantum information foundations or quantum ML, this is a proof-of-principle result showing indefinite causal order as a cryptographic resource with a genuinely novel detection mechanism distinct from standard BB84.
cards.summary: Researchers experimentally implemented a BB84-like QKD protocol placing Alice and Bob's operations in a photonic quantum SWITCH, achieving indefinite causal order. Eavesdropper detection is performed via control-qubit measurements rather than sacrificing key bits, achieving an average detection probability of 0.15±0.02 per shared qubit. A new measurement technique preserves path coherence while measuring photon polarization inside the SWITCH. Post-selection is still required, so this is not yet a fully secure QKD protocol.

cards.title: OmniScientist: End-to-End AI Scientist Handling Raw Multimodal Evidence Across 5 Discipline Families
cards.why_it_matters: The explicit test of raw perception vs. precomputed scalar features—with direct perception winning 85% of head-to-head judgments—is a concrete empirical result on why omni-modal grounding matters for autonomous research agents.
cards.summary: OmniScientist is an omni-modal AI scientist with a perception layer and three agents (ideation, experiment, writeup) operating in a deterministic pipeline. Evaluated on 36 real-data cases across 5 discipline families and modalities including images, signals, audio, video, 3D structures, and trajectories, it completes raw-data-to-manuscript in all 36 cases, scoring a mean of 6.3 overall. Against a blind variant receiving only precomputed scalar features, direct perception improves all 7 evaluation dimensions and wins 85% of head-to-head comparisons.

cards.title: AutoDesign: Meta-Harness Optimizer Beats Claude Design on Academic Poster Generation
cards.why_it_matters: The RSI-style loop—where a meta-optimizer iteratively improves a code agent's harness using rollout feedback—is a concrete instantiation of recursive self-improvement for agentic design tasks worth studying architecturally.
cards.summary: AutoDesign is a framework where a meta-harness optimizer directs a code agent to recursively improve its harness based on rollout feedback, applied to academic paper-to-poster generation. On PosterBench Main Track (100 papers, 5 disciplines), it scores 78.32, surpassing Claude Design by 7.45 points. Integrating the learned DesignHarness across 7 code-agent configurations raises average PosterBench Score from 54.99 to 67.39 (+12.4%). A full autonomous run completes in ~40 minutes for under $3.

cards.title: HumanTracker: 153-Hour Benchmark and HumanScore Metric for Perceptually Aligned Humanoid Motion Tracking
cards.why_it_matters: If you work on humanoid robotics or embodied AI evaluation, HumanScore's focus on contact and stability failures that kinematic metrics miss is directly relevant to building trackers that behave well in the real world.
cards.summary: HumanTracker introduces a humanoid motion tracking benchmark with ~153 hours of optical motion capture from multiple professional performers, organized into four motion families with text labels. HumanScore, trained on 12K motion pairs (24K motions), is a preference-aligned metric that better predicts human preferences than kinematic error metrics and specifically surfaces contact and stability failures—such as foot skating and mistimed touchdowns—that per-frame metrics miss.

cards.title: Defensive Booster: Single Algorithm Unifies Online Gradient Boosting and Weak-to-Strong Boosting Guarantees
cards.why_it_matters: For researchers working on online learning theory or robust forecasting, a single efficient algorithm that provably achieves both Brier score competitiveness and vanishing classification error—previously only available separately—is a clean theoretical contribution worth noting.
cards.summary: The Defensive Booster is an online probabilistic forecasting algorithm that simultaneously achieves two previously separate guarantees: Brier score competitiveness with the best predictor in the span of a weak hypothesis class (matching online gradient boosting rates), and vanishing randomized classification error under the smooth weak-learning condition (matching online classification boosting rates). It uses a single weak-class learner rather than large ensembles, yielding orders-of-magnitude faster runtime. A strongly adaptive variant extends both guarantees to every time interval.
